title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. There is an extension 1 → π → E → G → 1 and an element ρ ∈ E of finite order n that acts on π by conjugation. The 'équation des lacets' (8) is the cocycle equation g·ρ(g)·…·ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1. Its solutions are taken modulo π-ρ-conjugation, g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}. Equivalently they are π-conjugacy classes of splittings, i.e. the non-abelian H^1(Z/n, π).

Previous page. G^ρ = Centr_G(ρ̇). E_ρ is the inverse image of G^ρ in E, and E_ρ acts on these classes through G^ρ. A solution g can be written g = αρ(α)^{-1} with α ∈ E_ρ (rather than α ∈ π) exactly when [g]_ρ lies in the G^ρ-orbit of the trivial class [1]_ρ.

This page.
- The admissible images α̇ are exactly those satisfying α̇·[1]_ρ = [g]_ρ (27). For each such α̇ some lift α solves (26), g = αρ(α)^{-1}; Grothendieck notes this is a tautology.
- Uniqueness question. The solutions α ∈ E_ρ of (26) form a coset of the subgroup of α with αρ(α)^{-1} = 1, i.e. [α,ρ] = 1. That subgroup is E^ρ = Centr_E(ρ) ⊂ E_ρ (28).
- Since ρ ∈ E^ρ, this subgroup contains ⟨ρ⟩ ≅ Z/n. So uniqueness never holds, except in the degenerate case ρ = 1, which would force E = 1.
- Remedy. Assume π^ρ = {1}, i.e. E^ρ ∩ π = 1 (29). Then E^ρ → G^ρ ⊂ G is injective.
- Consequence, finished on the next page. Solutions α ∈ E_ρ of (26) correspond bijectively to their images α̇ in G, i.e. to the transporter of [1]_ρ into [g]_ρ under the G^ρ-action. Choosing an element of the transporter chooses α.

Application on the next page. Take π = π_1(U_{0,3}), E = the cartographic/Teichmüller extension, G = T_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Z/2. The classes of solutions are the two 'poles' −j, −j̄, i.e. the fixed points of ρ̇. Grothendieck then passes to E' = π·{1,τ_∞} with E'^ρ = 1, to study solutions of g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 in π_{0,3}. This is the order-3 relation familiar from the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / Drinfeld hexagon context.
errors: '(sauf dans le cas trivial où ρ^n=1 i.e. ρ=1)': the degenerate case is really n=1 (ρ of order 1). ρ^n=1 holds by assumption, so the phrasing is loose.
'les α ∈ E^ρ solutions de (26)' should read α ∈ E_ρ; elements of E^ρ only solve (26) for g=1.
The solution set is the left coset α·E^ρ (α' = αβ with β ∈ E^ρ). Grothendieck writes 'classe à droite', which is consistent only under the French naming convention; this is not a real error.
The bijection with the transporter is correct: injectivity uses π^ρ = 1, and surjectivity is the tautology (27).

ideas.what: Fibres of the map H^1(⟨ρ⟩,π) → H^1(⟨ρ⟩,E): solutions α of g = αρ(α)^{-1} form a coset of the centralizer E^ρ, and the class of g is described via the orbit of the trivial class under the centralizer G^ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Twisting and exact sequences of pointed sets in non-abelian group cohomology

ideas.what: Using the hypothesis π^ρ = 1 to identify lifts α with elements of the transporter in G^ρ.
Preparation for analysing solutions of g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 in π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) via the Teichmüller group T_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Order-3 relation in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (Drinfeld/Ihara)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT spirit); La Longue Marche

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine non-abelian cohomology bookkeeping (coset of a centralizer, transporter bijection) supporting a later computation. Nothing on this page is new.
transcription_corrections: 'ce groupe n'est autre que E' should read 'ce groupe n'est autre que E^ρ' (as defined in (28)).
'L'ensemble des cas α' is likely 'L'ensemble de ces α'.
'(ce qui est pure tautologie)' appears inside parentheses as 'Ce qui est pure tautologie'.
The (27) label belongs to the displayed relation α̇[1]_ρ = [g]_ρ.
